```{r}
library(tidyverse)
library(tidymodels)

# Load the processed data if it isn't already loaded
load("data/biomarker-clean.RData")

# Reproducible 80/20 train-test split
set.seed(101422)

split <- initial_split(
  biomarker_clean,
  prop = 0.8,
  strata = group
)

train <- training(split)
test  <- testing(split)

# Identify the protein columns
protein_names <- setdiff(
  names(train),
  c("group", "ados")
)

# Rank proteins using Welch's t-tests on TRAINING DATA ONLY
protein_ranking <- map_dfr(protein_names, function(protein) {

  test_result <- t.test(
    train[[protein]][train$group == "ASD"],
    train[[protein]][train$group == "TD"]
  )

  tibble(
    protein = protein,
    p_value = test_result$p.value
  )
}) %>%
  arrange(p_value)

# Function to fit and evaluate a model using the top k proteins
evaluate_panel <- function(k) {

  selected <- head(protein_ranking$protein, k)

  # Fit logistic regression on training subjects
  train_model <- train %>%
    select(group, all_of(selected)) %>%
    mutate(is_asd = as.integer(group == "ASD"))

  model <- glm(
    is_asd ~ . - group,
    data = train_model,
    family = binomial()
  )

  # Predict ASD probabilities for held-out test subjects
  test_model <- test %>%
    select(group, all_of(selected)) %>%
    mutate(
      truth = factor(group, levels = c("TD", "ASD")),
      prob = predict(model, newdata = ., type = "response"),
      predicted = factor(
        if_else(prob >= 0.5, "ASD", "TD"),
        levels = c("TD", "ASD")
      )
    )

  tibble(
    panel_size = k,
    proteins = paste(selected, collapse = ", "),
    accuracy = mean(test_model$predicted == test_model$truth),
    sensitivity = mean(
      test_model$predicted[test_model$truth == "ASD"] == "ASD"
    ),
    specificity = mean(
      test_model$predicted[test_model$truth == "TD"] == "TD"
    ),
    AUROC = yardstick::roc_auc(
      test_model,
      truth = truth,
      prob,
      event_level = "second"
    )$.estimate
  )
}

# Compare different panel sizes
simple_results <- map_dfr(
  c(3, 5, 10),
  evaluate_panel
)

print(simple_results)
```
